title: Wrath of God
definition: The wrath of God is His holy and righteous opposition to sin, evil, rebellion, and all that dishonors His glory.
summary: God's wrath is His just response to sin and evil.
christFocus: Jesus bore wrath for His people so that those who trust Him are saved from condemnation.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God's wrath is not sinful anger, moodiness, or cruelty. It is His holy opposition to evil. Because God is good, He cannot be indifferent toward sin.

The wrath of God reveals the seriousness of rebellion against Him. It also magnifies the love of Christ, who saves His people from wrath through His death and resurrection.

Those who trust Christ are not condemned, because He has borne what their sins deserved.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people want a God of love without a God who judges evil. The wrath of God matters because love without justice would leave evil unanswered and sin untreated.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not treat sin lightly. Flee to Christ for mercy, warn others with humility, and worship the Savior who rescues from wrath.
